title: grounded-ai-evals: a four-layer method for evaluating AI systems that answer with evidence
description:
A four-layer method for evaluating AI systems that are supposed to answer with evidence — retrieval-augmented assistants, knowledge-graph question answering, GraphRAG-style pipelines — together with a dependency-free Python reference implementation.

The layers are ordered so that each is only meaningful once the one above it holds: graph correctness, ontology hygiene, answer groundedness, and baseline comparison. The library computes citation precision and recall, unsupported rate, abstention split into correct and over-cautious, provenance coverage and judge agreement (Cohen's kappa), and renders a release gate that blocks on named checks rather than on a weighted mean.

The documentation maps the method to public standards and benchmarks (SHACL, OWL, OOPS!, OAEI, ALCE, FActScore, RAGAS, BFCL) and to the EU AI Act articles the resulting evidence serves.
